blocks.title: A namespace to limit
blocks.what: A LimitRange works inside one namespace, so the file starts by creating limits-demo.
blocks.why: A separate namespace keeps the rules away from your other lessons.
blocks.ifRemoved: The LimitRange has no namespace to live in, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: A namespace for the size rules
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: limits-demo

blocks.title: Add the LimitRange
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a LimitRange, from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: A LimitRange sets size rules for each container in its namespace.
blocks.ifRemoved: The file only creates the namespace.
blocks.comment: A second object: a LimitRange with size rules
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: limits-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange

blocks.title: Name and namespace
blocks.what: This LimitRange is called container-sizes and lives in limits-demo.
blocks.why: Its rules apply only to Pods created in limits-demo.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without the namespace, the rules land in your current namespace, usually default.
blocks.comment: The LimitRange’s name and the namespace it governs
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: limits-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: container-sizes
  namespace: limits-demo

blocks.title: Rules for containers
blocks.what: type: Container means the rules below apply to each container. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: A LimitRange can also set rules for whole Pods and for storage claims.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the LimitRange, because it needs at least one rule.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: limits-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: container-sizes
  namespace: limits-demo
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container

blocks.title: The largest size
blocks.what: max is the biggest CPU and memory limit a container may set.
blocks.why: It stops one container from asking for most of a node.
blocks.comment: No container may set a limit above this
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: limits-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: container-sizes
  namespace: limits-demo
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container
      max:
        cpu: 400m
        memory: 256Mi

blocks.title: Limits when none are set
blocks.what: default fills in the limits for a container that sets none.
blocks.why: Every container ends up with a limit, even when its author forgot.
blocks.ifRemoved: Containers that set no limits get the max instead: 400m CPU and 256Mi memory.
blocks.comment: Limits for containers that set none
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: limits-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: container-sizes
  namespace: limits-demo
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container
      max:
        cpu: 400m
        memory: 256Mi
      default:
        cpu: 300m
        memory: 128Mi

blocks.title: Requests when none are set
blocks.what: defaultRequest fills in the requests for a container that sets none.
blocks.why: The scheduler needs requests to place Pods well.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes uses the limit as the request, here 300m CPU and 128Mi memory.
blocks.comment: Requests for containers that set none
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: limits-demo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: container-sizes
  namespace: limits-demo
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container
      max:
        cpu: 400m
        memory: 256Mi
      default:
        cpu: 300m
        memory: 128Mi
      defaultRequest:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 64Mi

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API version. Namespaces and LimitRanges are both in the core v1 API.
notes.Namespace:kind: The type of object to create. A Namespace groups objects inside the cluster.
notes.LimitRange:kind: The type of object to create. A LimitRange sets size rules for its namespace.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.Namespace:metadata.name: The Namespace’s name. It must be unique in the cluster.
notes.LimitRange:metadata.name: The LimitRange’s name, used with kubectl describe limitrange.
notes.metadata.namespace: The namespace whose containers these rules apply to.
notes.spec: The desired state: the list of size rules.
notes.spec.limits: The rules. Each list item covers one type of object.
notes.spec.limits[].type: Container: each rule applies to each container on its own.
notes.spec.limits[].max: The largest limit a container may set. Bigger limits are rejected.
notes.spec.limits[].max.cpu: At most 400m: four tenths of a CPU core.
notes.spec.limits[].default: The limits given to a container that sets none.
notes.spec.limits[].default.cpu: A CPU limit of 300m when none is set.
notes.spec.limits[].default.memory: A memory limit of 128Mi when none is set.
notes.spec.limits[].defaultRequest: The requests given to a container that sets none.
notes.spec.limits[].defaultRequest.cpu: A CPU request of 100m when none is set.
notes.spec.limits[].defaultRequest.memory: A memory request of 64Mi when none is set.

tryIt.result: Prints namespace/limits-demo created and limitrange/container-sizes created.
A table shows the max, default request, and default limit for CPU and memory.
Starts a Pod that sets no sizes at all. Prints pod/plain-web created.
The LimitRange filled in the sizes: limits of 300m and 128Mi, requests of 100m and 64Mi.
Refused: the CPU and memory lesson’s Pod sets a 500m CPU limit, above the 400m max.

expect: pods "sized-web" is forbidden: maximum cpu usage per Container is 400m, but limit is 500m

tryIt.result: Deleting the namespace also deletes the LimitRange and the plain-web Pod.

questions.question: A container in limits-demo sets no CPU limit. What limit does it get?
questions.explain: default fills in missing limits. max only rejects limits that are too big.

questions.question: A container sets a CPU limit of 500m. What happens?
questions.explain: max is a hard rule. Kubernetes refuses the Pod and names the rule it broke.

questions.question: Does this LimitRange change Pods in the default namespace?
answers: No, only Pods created in limits-demo
questions.explain: A LimitRange works only in its own namespace, and only on Pods created after it.

fix.message: The LimitRange "container-sizes" is invalid: spec.limits[0].default[cpu]: Invalid value: "400m": default value 500m is greater than max value 400m
fix.explain: A default limit cannot be bigger than the max. Every container that used it would break the rule.
fix.fix: Lower the default CPU limit to 400m or less, such as 300m.

sources.title: Configure default CPU requests and limits for a namespace
